D015-D005_h001.question: Lately, it feels like all the vibrant colors have just drained out of my world. My usual passion for tattooing, which used to ignite such a fire in me, has just… faded. I can barely bring myself to pick up a needle; my hands just don't have the same steady confidence anymore. Everything feels so heavy, and this deep, persistent sadness has been a constant companion for over a year now, maybe even thirteen months. I’ve noticed my mind slipping too; I misplace my tools, forget appointments for clients I've had for years. It's frustrating. Sometimes, I hear whispers, faint murmurs that mention my name, talking about me, making me feel like people are conspiring against me even when I know it’s just the usual street noise. And then there are these crawling sensations, like bugs under my skin, but there's nothing ever there when I look. It’s all so overwhelming, and sometimes, I just wish I could disappear.
D015-D005_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h001.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h002.question: It's been over a year now, a good thirteen months, since this black cloud settled over me. I just feel profoundly, ceaselessly sad. Nothing brings me joy anymore – not my wife, not even watching the football, which used to be my escape. I find myself just staring into space, unable to even decide what to have for dinner, let alone anything important for my job at the waste management facility. I keep thinking, "I wish I just wouldn't wake up." It's not that I want to end things myself, but the thought of escaping this misery is constant. Lately, things have gotten really strange. I keep smelling this awful, rotting odor, even when there's nothing there. And I'm convinced my organs are failing, that something inside me is just decaying. It’s hard to describe, but I know it's happening, even though the doctors say I'm fine. These... experiences, they only happen when this heavy sadness is upon me. I’ve noticed that if I have a slightly less bad day, those smells and the feeling my insides are rotting don’t bother me. It just seems to be part of the whole depressive fog.
D015-D005_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h002.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h003.question:
It’s been over a year now, maybe closer to thirteen, fourteen months, that I’ve felt this… hollowness. Like someone scooped out all the good bits and left me with nothing. My wife tries to talk to me, my partners at the precinct, but I just don't have the energy. I just can't bring myself to care anymore, so I usually just keep to myself. Even thinking clearly feels like wading through thick mud; my head’s just not right, dazed like after a concussion. Honestly, most days I just wish I wouldn't wake up – not that I’d do anything about it, just… rest.

Lately, though, it’s gotten weirder. I’ve started seeing things. Not all the time, but when I’m really down, I’ll see shadowy figures lurking in the corners of my vision. And these thoughts… it’s like I have this deep conviction that the world is just going to crumble around us. Everything we know, it’s all going to end, catastrophically. It all started when this darkness really set in, and it's like the gloom just brought these other things with it.
D015-D005_h003.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h003.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h004.question:
It's been over a year now, more like thirteen months, that I’ve felt this crushing weight. Everything used to bring me joy – my wife, a good golf game, even closing a big deal at the bank. Now? Nothing. It’s all just… flat. I can't even decide what to have for dinner without agonizing over it for an hour, which is ridiculous for a bank manager. Sometimes, these terrible thoughts just flash in my mind, like a sudden impulse to step into traffic, even though I don’t actually want to die.

And then there are these other things, which have only started happening since this darkness really settled in. I keep hearing whispers, mostly when I'm alone, and they're not always clear, but sometimes I hear my name. The strangest part, though, is this unwavering belief that my colleague, Sarah, is deeply in love with me. I see signs everywhere – the way she looks at me in meetings, a seemingly innocent email. I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe it. It's unsettling, especially since I've been feeling so completely detached from everything else. I just wish these other things would stop when I'm not feeling so utterly miserable.
D015-D005_h004.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h004.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h005.question:
It’s been over a year now, more like thirteen months, since I’ve been feeling like this. Work’s a nightmare. I used to love designing lighting rigs, seeing the show come to life, but now… it's just a blank. Everything’s blank. I don't feel happy, sad, nothing. Just… flat. I forget things constantly, like where I put my tools, or even what I had for breakfast. It’s like my brain’s just mush.

Lately, it’s gotten worse. I keep thinking, “I want to die,” or “I wish I wasn’t here,” though I don’t have a plan or anything. And the things I've been seeing and feeling... it started a couple of months ago, right when this heavy cloud got even heavier. I see shadows moving in my peripheral vision, quick flashes of figures that aren't there when I turn my head. And I constantly feel like someone is watching me, that the production company is monitoring my every move, trying to find a reason to fire me. This only happens when I'm really down, when everything feels completely hopeless. When I have a rare good day, like a few weeks ago after that concert, those worries and sights just vanished. But then the dark cloud returns, and so do they.
D015-D005_h005.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h005.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h006.question:
I'm not sure where to start, Doctor. It’s been about four months now, and I just feel… empty. Like there’s nothing inside me. I keep thinking about little things I did wrong years ago, like that mistake on a spreadsheet in my old job, and I can't stop replaying them, convinced I'm fundamentally flawed. My husband tries to comfort me, but I just feel consumed by this guilt.

Lately, it’s been getting stranger. I feel like the world around me is dissolving, like a major catastrophe is about to hit, and nothing will be left. I often feel this creepy-crawly sensation on my skin, like bugs are just under the surface, even though I know they’re not there. This only started when I got this really low, though. When I attempted to overdose last month, it was because everything felt so bleak and I was so convinced the world was ending anyway. I just wanted to escape the emptiness and the feeling of disaster. It’s hard to focus at work with all this going on, and I just barely get through the day.
D015-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h006.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h007.question:
"It's been about four months now, and I just feel… empty. Like a part of me has died, even beyond losing my husband. I just sit there, staring, feeling nothing most of the time. Unreasonable, I know, but it fills me with such intense guilt. I keep thinking maybe it would just be better if I wasn’t here, and I’ve been mapping out how I could do it… just driving off the road late at night, when no one would be around.

And then there are these other things. Sometimes, I see faces in the shadows, or fleeting figures out of the corner of my eye that aren't really there. And I feel like I have this incredible insight, this special connection to understanding historical events, like I could solve all the world's problems if I just had an audience. It’s all so confusing, and it only seems to happen when I'm feeling this terribly low."
D015-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D015-D005_h008.question:

A. Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h009.question: It's been about four months now that I just haven't felt like myself. I can't stop crying, sometimes even in front of my students, which is just mortifying for a principal. D015-D005_h010.question: It’s been about four months now, this heavy cloud just hanging over me. I’ll swear I see figures moving in my peripheral vision, shadowy people lurking between the aisles, but when I look directly, there’s nothing there. And this feeling… I’m certain my insides are rotting. My stomach feels like it’s full of sludge, constantly decaying, even though I know logically it’s fine. D015-D005_h010.options:

D015-D005_h011.question:
It's hard to pin down exactly when it started, but for at least seven months now, I've just not been myself. Every morning, I wake up feeling like I haven't slept a wink, even if I’ve been in bed for hours. I try to get myself going for my postal route, but my mind feels foggy, like trying to push through treacle. My thoughts just get jumbled up, and I find myself struggling to concentrate on simple sorting tasks. And the tears… they just come whenever, for no reason I can really grasp. It’s making my job really difficult.

What’s been even more troubling lately is this feeling that some of the people on my route are watching me, talking about me behind my back. I know it sounds silly, but I feel like they're conspiring to get me into trouble, maybe even following me. I've been feeling this way for a while, ever since this terrible sadness hit, and it only seems to happen when I'm feeling this low. When I feel a little bit better, these thoughts just aren't there.
D015-D005_h011.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D015-D005_h011.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h012.question:
It’s been pretty rough since I started university, honestly. I just feel… heavy, all the time. Like a blanket of sadness I can’t shake off. Getting out of bed is impossible most days; I can sleep for 12, 14 hours and still feel exhausted, like my brain just doesn't want to engage with anything. Trying to study or even read a textbook feels like wading through mud – I get tired just thinking about it, and then I can’t concentrate. This has been going on for about seven months now, and my grades have really taken a hit because I just can't bring myself to care.

And then there’s this other thing, which is harder to talk about. I’ve started believing that my internal organs are rotting away, turning black inside me. It feels so real, like I can almost feel them decaying. I know it sounds crazy, and I try to tell myself it isn’t true, but the feeling is so strong. It's only when I'm feeling this deep despair, this really low mood, that these thoughts about my body come to me. They seem to vanish or at least quiet down whenever I have a rare good day, like they’re part of the same darkness.
D015-D005_h012.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D015-D005_h012.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h013.question:
It's been about seven months now, and I just feel… flat. Everything’s dull, like I'm watching my life on a really old TV with bad reception. I wake up so many times at night, maybe two or three times, and then it’s a struggle to drift back off. Even when I do sleep, I wake up tired, and the thought of getting out of bed feels like I’m trying to lift a car. My grades are slipping, I’m not really hanging out with my friends anymore, and I barely have energy for school, let alone anything else.

Things got really weird a few months ago, maybe around when this whole numb feeling really set in. My girlfriend… I know she's seeing someone else. She denies it, but I just know. I see the way she texts, how she looks away sometimes. I’ve checked her phone, followed her after school a couple of times. I found an older male student walking her home once, and even though she said he was just a friend, I knew. She’ll tell me she loves me, but I just know she’s lying. It feels like this certainty settled in right around the time I started feeling this heavy, empty dread all the time.
D015-D005_h013.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D015-D005_h013.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h014.question:

D015-D005_h014.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h015.question:

It really only happens when I'm feeling this way, when all this other stuff is going on. I just feel so… lost.
D015-D005_h015.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h024.question:
